question: A shared services team receives a request to use Claude for summarising supplier contracts. Which sequence best analyses the use case before any commitment is made?
options: A) Confirm the decision the summaries support; check the upload policy; try a handful of contracts; compare with trusted summaries.
B) Try a handful of contracts; confirm the decision the summaries support; check the upload policy; compare with trusted summaries.
C) Check the upload policy; compare with trusted summaries; confirm the decision the summaries support; try a handful of contracts.
D) Compare with trusted summaries; try a handful of contracts; confirm the decision the summaries support; check the upload policy.
correct_answers: A) Confirm the decision the summaries support; check the upload policy; try a handful of contracts; compare with trusted summaries.
explanations: Correct. Knowing which decision the summaries feed defines what they must contain, the policy check establishes whether the contracts may be uploaded at all, a small trial gives real evidence cheaply, and comparing against summaries the team already trusts shows whether the quality is good enough to commit to.

Trying contracts first means uploading material before anyone has checked whether that is permitted, and the trial is run without knowing what the summaries are for, so there is no basis for judging the results.
Comparing with trusted summaries before any have been produced is impossible, and confirming the purpose after that comparison leaves the trial run at the very end with nothing left to inform.

Starting with a comparison there is nothing to compare against, and leaving the policy check until last means the contracts have already been uploaded by the time anyone asks whether they should have been.
